thread:
Jorge: Hey team — customer reported daily usage dashboard for org `acme-prod` is showing a one-day shift in the chart and the CSV export rows appear to be grouped into the previous UTC day. They use Asia/Kathmandu (UTC+5:45).
Alex: yep, our billing shows 2026-03-15 usage in the dashboard but CSV rows have timestamp 2026-03-14 for many records.
Jorge: Thanks — can you paste one example row from the CSV? Also which org timezone is set in Console? :mag:
Alex: sample CSV row: `org_id,ts,product,tokens\nacme-prod,2026-03-14T18:12:00Z,text-gen,230` — Console timezone set to Asia/Kathmandu (Org settings -> Timezone: Asia/Kathmandu)
Maya: I've seen this before when exports are generated in UTC and then frontend daylight cutoff uses org tz. Need to confirm whether export pipeline applies org tz at grouping time or not.
Ethan: @Jorge can you capture a repro? Steps I want: 1) Org tz = Asia/Kathmandu 2) Generate traffic around midnight local (e.g., 23:50-00:10 local) 3) Request CSV export from Console and compare chart bucket.
Jorge: Repro steps I ran: I created synthetic hits at `2026-03-15T18:50:00Z` and `2026-03-15T19:05:00Z` (which map to 00:35 and 00:50 on 2026-03-16 in Asia/Kathmandu). Dashboard shows both under 2026-03-16, CSV placed both under 2026-03-15.
Li: digging into export job logs now. Looks like export pipeline uses `DATE(timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')` for grouping, then attaches org tz separately in metadata. The frontend chart uses `timestamp AT TIME ZONE '<org_tz>'::text` before bucketing. So mismatch if conversion order is reversed.
Ethan: can you paste the query? suspecting we do `DATE(utc_ts)` for export then `convert to org tz` for UI — that will shift day boundary differently than doing `DATE(utc_ts AT TIME ZONE org_tz)`.
Li: snippet from export job:
```
SELECT org_id, DATE(usage_ts) as day, SUM(tokens) FROM usage_events
WHERE org_id = 'acme-prod' AND usage_ts >= '2026-03-15'::date
GROUP BY 1,2;
```
That doesn't apply org tz. UI query does:
```
SELECT DATE(usage_ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kathmandu') as day_local, ...
```
So export is in UTC-day boundaries.
Maya: That's the root cause. Customers expect exports to match Console day boundaries when they set an org timezone.
Jorge: Proposed fix: change export pipeline to compute day using org tz, e.g. `DATE(usage_ts AT TIME ZONE org_tz)` — or add a config toggle. Can we patch for exports ASAP? :pray:
Ethan: I'll open a quick PR to switch to org-aware day bucketing in the export service. Short-term workaround: tell customer to set their billing window to UTC in Console until patch, or run local transform `SELECT usage_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kathmandu'` to reassign days.
Jorge: Communicating to customer: "we found mismatch in how CSV export buckets days (UTC) vs Console charts (org tz). Engineering working on a fix; ETA 2 business days. Temporary workaround: re-bucket CSV locally or switch org tz to UTC."
Alex: thanks — re-bucketing locally worked. Please keep me updated.
dev-deployer-bot: Deployment started for export-service:pr-591 -> staging :rocket:
Ethan: PR created: https://git.redwood/exports/pull/591 — changes `DATE(usage_ts)` -> `DATE((usage_ts AT TIME ZONE org_timezone))` and adds unit tests for multiple offsets incl. half-hour/45-minute zones.
Li: Added regression alert on nightly export job comparing export-day vs frontend-day for a sample of orgs. If mismatch > 0 for > 1% orgs, pager.
Jorge: Closing loop with customer in 24h after staging verification. Marking issue as "export-day-boundary-org-tz-mismatch" internally. :white_check_mark:
